description: Touch targets, safe areas, lists, forms, and feedback on small screens.

screens.body:
On desktop you aim with a pixel-precise cursor. On a phone you aim with a fingertip about 10mm wide — on a moving bus, one-handed. Touch targets need to be generous: around 44 points on iOS, 48dp on Android.

Crowded, tiny buttons cause mis-taps and rage. Space your tappable elements out and make the important ones big.

check.question: A comfortable minimum touch target is…

screens.heading: Fingers, not cursors
screens.keyPoint: Design for fingertips: big targets, generous spacing.

screens.body:
Phones have notches, camera cutouts, rounded corners, and home indicators eating into the screen edges. The safe area is the rectangle guaranteed free of all of that.

Keep buttons and text inside the safe area. Content that slides under a notch looks broken, and a button under the home indicator can't be tapped.

options: The region clear of notches and home indicators
check.question: The safe area is…

screens.heading: Safe areas and notches
screens.keyPoint: Keep interactive UI inside the safe area.

screens.body:
Most mobile screens are lists: feeds, chats, settings, search results. Lists scroll, so they can hold far more than fits on screen — but rendering ten thousand rows at once will choke the phone.

Use virtualized lists (FlatList in React Native, LazyColumn in Compose). They only render the rows on screen plus a small buffer, recycling rows as you scroll.

options: Only render the rows near the viewport
check.question: A virtualized list works by…

screens.heading: Lists carry mobile UI
screens.keyPoint: Virtualize long lists — render only what's visible.

screens.body:
Typing on glass is miserable, so every field you demand costs you users. Ask for the minimum, and make each field easy: show the right keyboard (numeric for PINs, email keyboard with @ for emails), enable autofill, and validate inline as they type.

Validate early and kindly — a red error after hitting submit, with no clue what was wrong, is how forms get abandoned.

options: Show the right keyboard and validate inline
check.question: A mobile-friendly form should…

screens.heading: Forms without the pain
screens.keyPoint: Fewer fields, right keyboards, inline validation.

screens.body:
On a phone, the user can't see your server thinking. Every tap needs acknowledgement within about 100 milliseconds — a pressed state, a spinner, a skeleton screen — or the user taps again, thinking nothing happened.

Use skeleton placeholders for loading content, spinners for short waits, and toasts or snackbars to confirm actions like 'Saved'. Silence feels like a bug.
screens.heading: Feedback is everything
screens.keyPoint: Acknowledge taps instantly; never leave the user guessing.

screens.body:
Small screens punish small text. Body text around 16–17pt stays readable at arm's length; anything much smaller forces zooming. Keep contrast strong — sunlight washes out weak greys.

Support both light and dark mode. Many users live in dark mode, and a blinding white screen at night is an instant delete.

options: As small as possible to fit more
check.question: Readable mobile body text is…

screens.heading: Readable on small screens
screens.keyPoint: Big-enough type, strong contrast, dark mode support.

screens.body:
Swipe-to-delete, pull-to-refresh, pinch-to-zoom — gestures are the mobile vocabulary. But hidden gestures are undiscoverable: if the only way to do something is a gesture nobody taught the user, it doesn't exist.

Keep core actions visible as buttons. Use gestures as shortcuts for things that also have a visible path, and teach them once with a hint.

options: Hide key actions behind secret gestures
Keep core actions visible; gestures are shortcuts
check.question: The safe rule for gestures is…

screens.heading: Gestures and scrolling
screens.keyPoint: Gestures are shortcuts, not the only path.
